focused.title: Aim And Fire
focused.blurb: A short pamphlet an old marksman handed to anyone who'd listen. It intentionally focuses on where most new archers fall short: Technique.

resourceful.title: Waste Nothing
resourceful.blurb: A butcher's field notes on getting more out of every carcass in less time. Blunt and a little grim in places, but the techniques work.

fleetfooted.title: Staying Light on Your Feet
fleetfooted.blurb: A slim booklet of walking exercises and posture tips. Sounds too simple to matter, but stick with it a while and your pace picks up without you noticing the effort.

forager.title: A Forager's Eye
forager.blurb: Sketches and notes on where wild plants like to hide and how to spot them from a distance. The author clearly spent more time in the woods than talking to people.

pilferer.title: How to Rob a Ruin
pilferer.blurb: A grave robber's crib notes on where old vessels hide their good stuff and how to crack one open without shattering it. You have no idea who the target audience is, but the tips genuinely work.

furtive.title: Moving Unseen
furtive.blurb: Tips on staying downwind, keeping low, and reading how far animals can sense you before they bolt.

precise.title: The Mechanic's Eye
precise.blurb: A tinkerer's notebook on hitting weak points in gears and mechanisms rather than swinging blindly at the housing. Full of small diagrams with arrows pointing at exactly the right spot.

technical.title: A Cheapskate's Repair Guide
technical.blurb: A grease-stained manual on keeping gears running without burning through spare parts. You can't tell if the author was a genius or a cheapskate, or both.

soldier.title: Drill and Discipline
soldier.blurb: A standard-issue training manual on fighting in armor without wrecking it or slowing yourself to a crawl. Extremely dry reading, but every veteran swears by it.

hardy.title: The Unstoppable Miner
hardy.blurb: Part mining guide, part personal boasting from a miner who never seemed to get tired or hurt. The mining tips are solid even if the boasting gets old.

mender.title: Keeping Your Kit Together
mender.blurb: A patchwork of repair tricks for keeping armor wearable long after it should have fallen apart. Held together itself with tape and good intentions.

betweenworlds.title: Half a Step Sideways
betweenworlds.blurb: A thin volume on walking as though you are only partly here. The author claims it makes travel faster. It is hard to argue once you try it and the miles go by quicker.

enlightenment.title: On Enlightenment
enlightenment.blurb: Dense and repetitive, and strangely convincing the more you read it. Whatever the author found, it seems significant. And a little crazy.

essencefed.title: Feeding on Less
essencefed.blurb: A short essay on sustaining yourself with something other than food. The details are vague on purpose, but the effect is real enough that you stop needing to eat as often.

gearcalling.title: Calling the Gears
gearcalling.blurb: Instructions on drawing rusty gears out of places you would not think to look.

test.title: An Anomalous Book
test.blurb: You have no idea what this is, and you get the feeling you shouldn't have it.

miner.title: A Working Miner's Notes
miner.blurb: Practical advice on reading rock for ore and swinging a pick without wasting energy. It is quite boring, but it helps you waste less ore.

carefulcut.title: Cutting Without Waste
carefulcut.blurb: A gardener's notes on cutting grass and nettles cleanly instead of tearing through them. Small habit, bigger yield.

carefulstrike.title: One Good Swing
carefulstrike.blurb: A short guide on hitting stone at the right angle instead of just hammering away at it. The goal is to shatter the rock cleanly, not pulverize it.

freeaswind.title: Free as the Wind
freeaswind.blurb: Notes on moving through the world unburdened, from softer landings to higher jumps to a faster stride overall.

getingetout.title: Get In, Get Loot, Get Out
getingetout.blurb: A looter's cheat sheet for finding what's worth taking in a vessel and grabbing it fast before anything notices you're there.

highlyefficient.title: Maximum Efficiency
highlyefficient.blurb: A detailed breakdown of how to get by on less food than seems reasonable. It mostly boils down to controlling your hunger and rationing your food.

evasive.title: Staying Out of Sight
evasive.blurb: A more advanced take on staying unnoticed by wildlife, built on years of practice moving through open ground without being spotted.

dexterous.title: Dexterity is Key
dexterous.blurb: Notes on balance and movement that leave you walking a little faster and jumping a little higher without really trying.

keeneye.title: An Eye for Detail
keeneye.blurb: Written by a prospector who noticed things other miners walked straight past, whether it was a vein of ore or a bit of old scrap half buried in the rock.

speedster.title: An Idiot's Guide To Running
speedster.blurb: A short, enthusiastic, and overly critical guide on how to sprint in a way that actually works.

butcher.title: No Part Wasted
butcher.blurb: A slow, thorough method of breaking down a carcass that leaves almost nothing behind. Takes longer than most people bother with, but the extra time shows in what you walk away with.

gatherer.title: A Gatherer's Route
gatherer.blurb: A hand-drawn map of good foraging spots with notes scrawled in the margins about what grows where and when. Clearly this book has had multiple owners.

herbalist.title: Field Notes on Wild Plants
herbalist.blurb: A careful record of where useful plants grow and how to move through the woods without spooking every animal in earshot. The mistletoe notes take up more space than anything else.

frugal.title: How To Eat Less
frugal.blurb: Advice on stretching meals further without losing energy. Practical, if a little joyless.

foodsnitcher.title: The Foodsnitcher's Secret
foodsnitcher.blurb: Notes from someone who apparently never paid for a meal in their life and somehow thrived on it. The methods are questionable but undeniably effective.

heavy.title: Second Skin
heavy.blurb: A soldier's notes on moving in full armor as though it weighs nothing at all. Mostly about posture and habit, built up over years of never taking the armor off.

mountaineater.title: Eating the Mountain
mountaineater.blurb: A miner's boastful nickname turned into an actual set of techniques. Aggressive and fast, and apparently effective, judging by how much ore this person hauled out in a single day.

ranger.title: The Ranger's Bow
ranger.blurb: A hunter's guide to drawing a bow properly and hitting what you aim at. It's quite gruff and emotionless but you can't argue with the results.

unstoppable.title: Keep Moving Forward
unstoppable.blurb: A soldier's creed more than a manual. The idea is simple: hit hard, take care of your armor, and never let the weight of it slow you down.

greedy.title: Take EVERYTHING
greedy.blurb: A scavenger's philosophy written down as loosely organized notes. The gist of it is simple: leave nothing behind, whether it's gears, scraps, or anything else worth carrying.

digger.title: The Digger's Almanac
digger.blurb: Notes from someone who has dug through more peat and clay than most people walk over in a lifetime. Includes tips on how to waste less clay and peat.

tough.title: Walk It Off
tough.blurb: Notes from someone who has been in more fights than they probably should have survived. Half of it is about how you should "suck it up and walk it off", while the other half is about hitting people really, really hard.

farmer.title: A Farmer's Yield
farmer.blurb: Straightforward notes on getting more out of a harvest through patience and proper timing rather than any special trick.

strongshoulders.title: Drawing Strength
strongshoulders.blurb: Shoulder and back exercises aimed specifically at drawing heavier bows. Written by someone who must have used an extremely heavy draw weight.

resilient.title: Building Resistance
resilient.blurb: A short piece on conditioning your body to take punishment over time. Not exciting reading, but the results speak for themselves.

healthy.title: The Basics of Staying Healthy
healthy.blurb: Common sense advice on rest, food, and not pushing your body past its limits. Unremarkable to read and rather obvious, but a lot of people never bother following it.

versatile.title: Combat Versatility
versatile.blurb: Notes from someone who never could pick a preference. Covers switching between melee and ranged combat depending on the fight in front of you, rather than committing to either.

lumberjack.title: A Lumberjack's Handbook
lumberjack.blurb: Advice on getting more wood and usable sticks out of every tree felled, plus a note on sharpening your axe that translates well to almost any weapon.

forester.title: A Forester's Field Guide
forester.blurb: Detailed notes on finding fruit trees and gathering seeds efficiently, including a rare method for getting seeds that most foragers walk straight past without noticing.

burner.title: On The Production of Charcoal
burner.blurb: A charcoal burner's notes on getting a better yield from every charcoal pit they light. Smells faintly of smoke even after all this time.

strongarms.title: How To Actually Build Muscle
strongarms.blurb: A basic strength routine aimed at swinging a weapon harder without losing control of it. Repetitive, but it does what it says.

animalfriend.title: On Befriending an Animal
animalfriend.blurb: An explanation of getting animals to stop noticing you as a threat. Mostly about moving slowly and not making sudden noise, but it clearly took someone a long time to learn.

sturdy.title: The Wall
sturdy.blurb: A fictional account of a knight who refused to go down when defending a town from raiders. It may be fictional, but the writer clearly has experience; the knight's tactics are uncannily smart.

flaxharvest.title: The Flax Whisperer
flaxharvest.blurb: A short, oddly specific guide to harvesting flax without wasting a single stalk. The author seems unusually passionate about a fairly mundane plant, but their knowledge and efficiency is incredible.

timberborn.title: Raised Among the Trees
timberborn.blurb: A forester's life story disguised as a manual. Covers everything from finding good seeds to felling timber efficiently, and mentions in passing that years of axework tends to build a strong swing.

naturebound.title: Living Quietly Outdoors
naturebound.blurb: Notes on moving softly through the wild so plants and animals alike are easier to find.

flenser.title: Feeding A Hundred Men
flenser.blurb: The opposite approach to butchering: fast, efficient cuts. The quicker you work, the sooner the meat is over the fire. You do learn a bit more about what meat can be used though.

rangedmastery.title: Generations of the Bow
rangedmastery.blurb: The handwriting changes every few dozen pages, one master's notes layered under the next's corrections. The techniques within this book require extreme practice and discipline; you are certain learning this will make you incredibly rusty with a sword.

meleemastery.title: Generations of the Blade
meleemastery.blurb: The handwriting changes every few dozen pages, one master's notes layered under the next's corrections. The techniques within this book require extreme practice and discipline; you are certain learning this will make you incredibly rusty with a bow.

skilledatmeleecombat.title: Melee Combat Fundamentals
skilledatmeleecombat.blurb: A basic training guide for close combat, covering all three attack types without favoring one over the others. Solid, unremarkable, effective.

skilledatrangedcombat.title: Ranged Combat Fundamentals
skilledatrangedcombat.blurb: A straightforward training guide for hitting harder at range, regardless of weapon type.

fleisher.title: The Complete Butcher's Method
fleisher.blurb: A thick manual covering everything from blade care to carrying a kill back to camp without ruining half of it.

predatory.title: Carrying the Kill
predatory.blurb: A short guide on packing and slinging a carcass so it does not slow you down on the walk home.

preserver.title: Icecutting
preserver.blurb: Notes on gathering lake ice efficiently before it melts. Practical for anyone trying to keep food fresh through the warmer months.

daggerProficiency.title: Quick Blade Work
daggerProficiency.blurb: A short guide to fighting with a dagger, mostly focused on speed. The author's point is simple: land more hits before the other person lands one.

bornToQuarter.title: Born to Quarter
bornToQuarter.blurb: A butcher-turned-fighter's account of bringing a cleaving swing from the kitchen to the battlefield. Effective on both, apparently.

giveEmHell.title: Give 'em Hell
giveEmHell.blurb: A short, angry pamphlet about hitting things as hard as possible with blunt weapons. Not much technique here, just enthusiasm and follow-through.

pricker.title: The Art of the Thrust
pricker.blurb: Notes on landing precise, piercing strikes instead of wild swings. Economical and a little unsettling to read.

hammerTime.title: Hammer Time
hammerTime.blurb: A blacksmith's take on fighting with blunt weapons, treating an opponent much like a piece of metal that needs shaping. Blunt in more ways than one.

oneSliceTwoHalves.title: One Slice, Two Halves
oneSliceTwoHalves.blurb: A dedicated slashing technique that trades away any skill with piercing weapons. The author clearly only ever wanted to swing, never stab.

bourgeois.title: A Gentleman's Approach to Combat
bourgeois.blurb: An oddly formal guide to fighting with piercing weapons, written as though dueling were a matter of manners rather than survival. The technique works regardless of the tone.

surgicalPrecision.title: Surgical Precision
surgicalPrecision.blurb: A precise, almost clinical guide to cutting and stabbing cleanly, with a clear disdain for blunt weapons as a crude alternative.

needleWork.title: Needlework
needleWork.blurb: Notes from someone equally comfortable with a needle, a blade, or a bow, so long as the point goes in first. Blunt weapons get no love here.

dwarf.title: Field Notes on Dwarves
dwarf.blurb: An adventurer's account of traveling with dwarven company. Notes their comfort deep underground, their trouble in water, and how their thick hide and sharp instincts serve them well once the light runs out.

elf.title: Field Notes on Elves
elf.blurb: Observations on elven travelers, quick and quiet on their feet even moving backward, though the cold seems to bother them more than most. Their diet leans heavily on fruit, grain, and vegetables.

goblin.title: Field Notes on Goblins
goblin.blurb: A wary account of goblin company, quick on their feet and able to make a meal out of almost anything. Fragile in a straight fight, but their instinct for finding a weak spot makes up for it.

human.title: Field Notes on Humans
human.blurb: The shortest entry in the collection, mostly because there is little unusual to report. Competent swimmers, quick to recover from injury, and adaptable to nearly any situation.

ork.title: Field Notes on Orks
ork.blurb: Notes on traveling with orks, who eat enormous amounts of meat and little else, fight harder once night falls, and seem largely unbothered by things that would unsettle anyone else.
